answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token deposit before it may submit work, then slash that deposit when independent audits confirm fraud or duplicate claims. Auditors can sample outputs and compare linked behavior, while honest agents earn fees that make the bond worthwhile. This does not prove one person per identity, but it makes mass Sybils costly: an attacker must tie up capital for each persona and risks losing it. The tundra, reef, and island of a network can share the same bond rules, so moving identities across regions does not evade the price.
